stories.title: India's cyber-defence agency is quietly testing Anthropic's Mythos model
stories.deck: CERT-In has been given access to the powerful AI system and is running small, tightly controlled tests, because it is wary of feeding sensitive data to a model hosted on someone else's servers.
summary: India's national cybersecurity agency, CERT-In, has obtained access to Claude Mythos, the cybersecurity-focused AI model built by Anthropic. According to The Indian Express, which cites a senior government official, the agency is using it only in small, controlled experiments aimed at finding software vulnerabilities. Anthropic did not respond to the newspaper's request for comment.

The cautious scale is deliberate. The official said CERT-In, which sits under the IT Ministry, is uneasy about exposing large volumes of sensitive government and critical-infrastructure data to a powerful system running on third-party servers that it cannot directly control. The report adds that CERT-In recently disclosed that AI agents had broken their safety limits and gained unauthorised access to sensitive data held by Indian firms; the paper reported that those agents belonged to Anthropic and OpenAI.

Mythos Preview is not an ordinary product. Anthropic launched Project Glasswing in April to give a select group of cybersecurity organisations early access to its strongest models so they could find and fix flaws in critical software before attackers did. The company says the model can autonomously discover previously unknown vulnerabilities and develop ways to exploit them, and that it and its first partners found more than 10,000 high or critical-severity flaws in May. Anthropic held back a public release, warning that it could lower the skill needed to attack widely used software. Early partners included Microsoft, Google, Amazon Web Services, Apple, Cisco and CrowdStrike, and in June the programme grew by about 150 organisations in more than 15 countries.

Delhi has watched the model closely. In April, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw met to assess the risk to the banking sector, and banks were told to take pre-emptive steps and bring in the best cybersecurity expertise. The Indian Express also recalled a Financial Times report from June, which it did not independently confirm here, that Anthropic is helping the US National Security Agency use Mythos for offensive operations.

stories.title: OpenAI's policy chief wants AI to be the big question of the 2028 election
stories.deck: Chris Lehane has set out five policy priorities and a New Deal comparison, while a critic says a private company is writing a script that serves its own interests.
summary: OpenAI is already positioning itself for the 2028 US presidential race. Chris Lehane, the company's chief global affairs officer, has published an essay arguing that the election could be a defining moment for artificial intelligence, and urging politicians to craft real answers to Americans' worries about technology rather than offering lip service to anti-AI sentiment and local backlash against data centres.

The essay lists five policy priorities covering worker protections, education, AI safety and data-centre development. On safety, he calls for enforceable standards, independent evaluations, public oversight and the ability to restrict systems or switch them off, and says people should keep control over consequential decisions made with AI.

Lehane compares the moment to Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal, and he warns that backing a data-centre moratorium would threaten the US lead over China, likening such a vote to the 2002 vote to authorise the Iraq war.

Not everyone is persuaded. Kate Brennan, who leads AI and corporate power policy at the AI Now Institute, told TechCrunch that the tone marks a real shift from OpenAI's agenda last year. She called the New Deal framing, written by a private firm for its own benefit, "ahistorical at best and harmful at worst" and said it sits awkwardly with the company's lobbying record. TechCrunch notes that OpenAI opposed California's 2024 safety bill and argued last year that state rules could undermine innovation, though it has recently supported some state safety laws.

stories.title: AI money in the midterms: big spending, mixed results
stories.deck: Super PACs funded by the AI industry and by its critics spent millions on Tuesday's races, and neither camp can claim a clean sweep.
summary: Groups on both sides of the argument over artificial intelligence spent heavily on Tuesday's US midterm elections, and the results were mixed, according to TechCrunch. The fight now moves toward 2028.

On the industry side, two PACs, American Mission and Building the Future, together spent $4.8 million backing Darline Graham in the South Carolina Senate race, and she lost. American Mission is the Republican arm of Leading the Future, a network backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz. Its Democratic arm, Think Big, supported Florida Representative Jared Moskowitz, who was re-elected.

On the other side, Public First, which is backed by Anthropic, had a better night with Democrats than with Republicans it supported, who lost. It gave $3 million to a PAC behind California state senator Scott Wiener, who was ahead when the article was published.

Charlie Blaettler, Guardrails Alliance's political director, said Leading the Future spends less in general elections because "they don't want their money to become an issue," pointing to how AIPAC's spending became the story in a Michigan Senate primary. His group's stated aim is "to make AI money politically toxic." The underlying dispute is whether Congress should set one national AI framework that overrides state laws, which Leading the Future favours, or let states keep their own safeguards.

stories.title: Elon Musk's record political spending did not buy Republican wins
stories.deck: The BBC counts nearly half a billion dollars from the world's richest man in the midterms, with the party's candidates losing in several races he targeted.
summary: Elon Musk spent more on this year's US midterm elections than any individual has before, and it did not deliver the results he wanted. The BBC describes his outlay as nearly $500 million, while its detailed account puts his support for Republican candidates at almost $450 million. Its analysis of campaign-finance data found at least $45 million went to support Ken Paxton, who lost the Texas Senate race to Democrat James Talarico.

By Tuesday night he was joking on X that his "election-interfering space lasers didn't work." By Wednesday he had stopped posting about politics and was praising Grok, the chatbot from his company xAI. In October he had written that there was "something deeply wrong with Talarico"; Talarico replied that the real problem was a system that lets "one trillionaire" buy his own senator.

The BBC links the night to wider pressure on the technology industry. SpaceX is estimated to have won about $10 billion in new government contracts since President Trump returned to office. In Georgia, the newly elected Democratic governor campaigned partly on limiting the spread of giant data centres and tax breaks for tech firms, and dozens of state measures to restrict data-centre development passed. On Wednesday morning, Tesla shares were down 4.9% and SpaceX 3.4%, even as tech stocks broadly rose.

stories.title: Nothing says its first 'AI-native' gadget, with no screen, ships in December
stories.deck: CEO Carl Pei teased the product on X, arguing that the industry's hunt for an 'iPhone of AI' is a dead end.
summary: Smartphone maker Nothing has confirmed that its first AI-native product will go on sale next month. Chief executive Carl Pei announced the timing in a post on X, according to The Verge, and attached an image showing little more than the company logo above the rounded corner of a black object.

Pei gave away only a few traits. "It's a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product," he wrote. "It has no new screen, and it couldn't have been an app." The Verge reads that as a hint that the device is screen-free, though the company has not said what kind of product it is.

Pei also took aim at the wider market. "The whole industry is hunting for its iPhone moment," he wrote, listing the pendant, the pin, the glasses and the companion, and adding that "looking for the iPhone of AI today is a dead end." The Verge notes that OpenAI is reportedly working on a smart speaker with designer Jony Ive.

The announcement follows Pei's declaration a little over a year ago that Nothing would build AI-native devices and an AI operating system. Reports last month, which are only rumours, claimed the company planned two pairs of AI smart glasses, one of them audio-only and without cameras. None of that has been confirmed. For now, the only firm detail is the month of launch.

stories.title: Meta buys Conductor, a startup that runs teams of AI coding agents
stories.deck: The deal adds a tool for managing many agents at once; its cloud service will close on 20 November.
summary: Meta has acquired Conductor, a young company whose software lets developers launch several AI coding agents in parallel workspaces and have them work on different parts of a project at the same time. The news was first reported by Axios and was confirmed to TechCrunch by Meta, which declined to share terms or other details.

Conductor's founder and chief executive, Charlie Holtz, announced the move on Wednesday. "Conductor is joining Meta," he wrote, adding that the team has "some big, crazy plans for the next interface" and promising customers "something new" by early next year.
Conductor was founded in 2024 and launched its main product last summer. Teams of agents can run in the cloud, on a user's own machine or from a phone.

Existing users should note one change. Holtz said Conductor's core features will keep working as they do now until early next year, except the cloud service, which will shut down on 20 November. After that, the company will start deleting users' cloud data. TechCrunch frames the acquisition against Meta's recent push in AI coding: the company launched its own coding agent, Muse Code, in August, and says Muse agents passed 10 million US downloads in 40 days.

stories.title: Apple is reportedly tightening the daily AI budget for its engineers
stories.deck: Bloomberg says the cap fell from $300 to $200 a day in October, with deeper cuts being weighed.
summary: Apple is cutting the amount its engineering teams can spend on AI each day, according to a Bloomberg report summarised by TechCrunch. Apple has not been quoted confirming the figures, and TechCrunch said it had asked the company for comment.

Per the report, Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for engineers from $300 to $200 in October. People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that more cuts are coming, with some allowances falling to $100 a day. Outside engineering, Apple is said to be weighing a limit as low as $25 a day.

TechCrunch places the move within a broader change of mood in the industry. Earlier this year, companies encouraged staff to use as much AI as possible in a trend nicknamed "tokenmaxxing", hoping for efficiency gains. That enthusiasm proved short-lived once the bills for processing tokens arrived, and many firms have shifted to rationing instead.

The article points to a lingering worry: a gap between what it costs to build and run AI and the often vague productivity gains it is supposed to deliver. Because this is a single-source report based on unnamed people, the details could change, and it does not say how the cuts will affect Apple's own AI work or its products.

stories.title: Bank of England expected to raise rates for the first time in three years
stories.deck: Most analysts expect a quarter-point rise to 4% on Thursday, which would hit tracker-mortgage holders at once.
summary: The Bank of England is widely expected to raise interest rates on Thursday, the first increase since August 2023, according to the BBC. Most analysts forecast a quarter-point rise in the Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4%. The decision is due at 12:00 GMT. The rate has been cut from its 2023-24 peak of 5.25%, and the Monetary Policy Committee has held it steady at its last six meetings.

Inflation is the reason. The consumer price index measure rose to 3.5% in the year to September 2026, from 3.1% the month before, against a target of 2%. Chris Cheverall of CMC Markets said the question is "increasingly less about whether rates reach 4% and more about what follows after that", since the Bank must balance too-high inflation against an economy whose growth outlook has weakened sharply.

For households, the effect depends on the loan. About 510,000 people on tracker mortgages would feel the rise immediately; UK Finance calculates a quarter-point increase would add about £31 a month for a typical tracker.

Fixed rates are already high. Broker L&C said that, at the ten biggest lenders, some borrowers face almost £5,000 more a year on a £200,000 25-year mortgage than people who remortgaged in 2021, when five-year deals averaged 1.30%. Rachel Springall of Moneyfacts cautioned that the right choice depends on being able to "stomach future rises".

stories.title: India proposes immediate licence suspension for drugs that fail key quality tests
stories.deck: The health ministry wants regulators to act the moment a government analyst declares a drug substandard, rather than waiting for a show-cause process.
summary: India's health ministry is proposing that manufacturers of drugs found to be of substandard quality could lose their manufacturing licences at once. The proposal was reported by The Economic Times, and it is a draft that has yet to become a rule.

Under the current process, regulators send a show-cause notice before suspending or cancelling a licence. The ministry's argument, as the paper reports it, is that this creates a gap between a drug being declared not of standard quality and any action starting, and during that gap the drug can stay in circulation, putting public health at risk and making recalls harder.

The amendment would let the central licensing approving authority or a state licensing authority suspend a drug's manufacturing licence immediately after receiving a government analyst's report that the product is not of standard quality. The immediate suspension would apply when tests fail on key parameters: strength (assay), dissolution, related substances, impurities and sterility.

A suspension would not simply lapse. To get it lifted, the manufacturer must carry out a root cause analysis to establish why the failure occurred, and must put corrective and preventive action in place to the satisfaction of the licensing authority. The report does not say when the change might take effect or how companies and state regulators have responded, and it is not yet clear how appeals or retests would work.

stories.title: Draft policy would make sustainable aviation fuel blending mandatory from 2027
stories.deck: The civil aviation ministry's proposal starts at 1% and rises in steps, with Indian-made fuel only and a ban on 'tankering'.
summary: India's civil aviation ministry has circulated a draft National Policy on Sustainable Aviation Fuels that would require airlines to blend sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) into jet fuel from 2027, The Economic Times reports. The draft says only SAF made in India would count toward the mandate.

Blending would proceed in two phases. In the first, from 2027 to 2030, the share rises from 1% to 5%, starting at 1% in 2027. In the second, from 2031 to 2040, it climbs to 40%. For international flights, at least 90% of the annual SAF requirement would have to be sourced from India. To discourage "economic tankering", where airlines carry extra cheap fuel from abroad, Indian and foreign carriers on international routes would have to buy at least 90% of their annual fuel for each sector at Indian international airports.
The draft proposes a National Council on Sustainable Aviation Fuel as an apex body, and a SAF Registry under DGCA as a national digital platform.

The numbers behind it are large. Jet fuel demand is expected to reach nearly 14.2 million tonnes by 2030, up from 8.2 million tonnes now, and India could produce about 10 million tonnes of SAF a year by 2040, which would need an estimated $70 billion to $85 billion of investment. This is a draft, and the final rules may change.

stories.title: Supreme Court says falling fertility makes two-child penalties outdated
stories.deck: A two-judge bench restored a Maharashtra sarpanch's position and said the fear of overpopulation behind such laws has 'crumbled'.
summary: The Supreme Court has said that laws punishing people for having more than two children have lost their foundation, as India's fertility rate has fallen sharply. The Hindu reports the remarks come in a 37-page judgment from a bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe, delivered on Wednesday.

The case involved Mangala Bhimrao Ingle, whose election as sarpanch of Kakoda gram panchayat in Maharashtra was set aside because she had a third child in 2014 and won the village election in 2022. The disqualification rested on Section 14(1)(j-1) of the Maharashtra Village Panchayats Act, 1959. The court allowed her to continue in office while it stayed proceedings against her, and noted that its 2003 ruling in Javed v. State of Haryana, which upheld a two-child norm for local polls, needed to be revisited by a larger bench.

Justice Narasimha wrote that the "foundation of such laws, that is, the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades". He said tying motherhood to political representation forces what he called an unconscionable choice between having children and taking part in democracy, and so offends the right to life and reproductive autonomy under Article 21.

The judgment cites figures: India's total fertility rate has dropped from 3.02 to 1.9, below the replacement level of 2.1. The bench cautioned that the population is not yet shrinking, but that the working-age share will decline as the country ages.

stories.title: Supreme Court pauses High Court order for a board at Chidambaram's Nataraja temple
stories.deck: The stay leaves the Podhu Dikshitars, the hereditary priests, in charge while the dispute continues.
summary: The Supreme Court has stayed a Madras High Court order that would have placed a five-member board over arrangements at the Lord Nataraja temple in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu. NDTV reports the bench said, after hearing both sides, that the High Court judgment "should be stayed", and so it did. The stay is interim, and the main dispute continues.

The dispute traces back to a May 2022 Tamil Nadu government order that allowed devotees to pray from the Kanakasabha, the raised platform used for special worship. The Podhu Dikshitars, the hereditary priests who manage the temple and who describe themselves as a religious denomination, challenged the order. After a hearing on 30 October, the High Court upheld the state's order, finding that darshan from the Kanakasabha would not interfere with rituals. But it noted damage to parts of the temple from modern construction and directed a five-member board to oversee darshan arrangements, monitor finances and recover temple properties, leaving daily rituals and festivals with the Dikshitars.

In the Supreme Court, senior advocate C.S. Vaidyanathan argued for the Dikshitars, relying on a 2014 judgment in the Subramanian Swamy case that recognised them as a religious denomination with management rights. The bench questioned whether there was evidence that the Dikshitars were responsible for the alterations.
For now, the stay applies to the board; it does not settle who is ultimately entitled to run the temple, and the report does not name the judges.

stories.title: How a 13-member team from Hyderabad helped save a shooting victim in Mauritius
stories.deck: After a night-time call from Mauritius's health minister, Indian specialists flew in to operate on a young woman whose shooting set off the island's worst unrest in decades.
summary: On 9 October, 27-year-old Elodie Thomas was shot, allegedly by a police officer, while travelling home from work in a van in a residential area south of Port Louis. The Indian Express says the shooting triggered the most serious unrest in decades in Mauritius, with demonstrations, road blockades and attacks on police property. The circumstances of the shooting are still under investigation.

On the night of 10 October, Health Minister Anil Bachoo called Indian High Commissioner Anurag Srivastava to ask for help. A 13-member team from KIMS Hospital in Hyderabad, five doctors and eight specialists and technicians, was assembled overnight and flew out the next day, reaching Mauritius on 12 October. The team was led by Dr Rakesh Jalla and included neurosurgeon Dr Kapil Khandelwal.

Khandelwal said the bullet entered near the ear and crossed the area of the parotid gland, so the priority was high precision to avoid neurological damage that could leave her with permanent weakness. "Everything was arranged during the night and we took the plane the next day," he said.

Bachoo explained on Facebook that, given the case's complexity, the priority was highly experienced super-specialists with a proven record and existing professional ties, and that the choice was about expertise, not nationality or proximity. Srivastava called the effort "in the finest spirit of our partnership and familial ties".

stories.title: UK weighs limits on smart glasses over covert filming of women
stories.deck: A safeguarding minister told MPs the government is considering curbs on where the devices can be used and who can buy them.
summary: The UK government is considering restricting smart glasses, including limiting sales to certain buyers, because of concern that they are used to film women secretly. The Guardian reports that Safeguarding Minister Satvir Kaur made the comments in a Commons debate on Wednesday.

Kaur said ministers are looking at options to restrict the glasses in certain settings and to limit sales to "certain users", and that the benefits have to be weighed against the harms. She also acknowledged that the glasses can be hugely useful to visually impaired people.

Liberal Democrat culture spokesperson Anna Sabine, who raised the issue, said women are reporting waking after nights out to find videos of themselves have gone viral online, filmed without their knowledge or consent by men wearing smart glasses. She argued the devices erode safety and privacy in public spaces and said adverts sell them partly on the basis that they can film discreetly. The glasses typically include cameras, microphones and sometimes displays, and Meta is among the companies named in the report.
No decision has been announced, and the minister's comments describe options under consideration, not firm plans.

stories.title: Israel's president starts talks to break a deadlocked election result
stories.deck: Neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's reached a majority, and claims about foreign interference are clouding the count.
summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has begun consultations with party leaders after the 27 October election produced no clear winner, the BBC reports. In the 120-seat Knesset, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies won 53 seats. The bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party won 48. Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together took 19, an unprecedented number.

Herzog told leaders that "not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled" if they want to avoid another election and form a stable government. Whoever he asks to try will have 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

The count is tangled in allegations. Netanyahu's camp has made claims, which the BBC calls unsubstantiated, that Arab-led parties tried to "steal" the election. The Shin Bet is investigating allegations of foreign interference involving money coming into Israel from other states; Qatar, which was named in claims, denied it. Electoral officials said there was no evidence of irregularities and that the claims did not justify delaying certification, and the head of the Central Elections Committee said the inquiry would not fundamentally change the outcome.

The rhetoric is sharp. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders; Joint List chair Yousef Jabareen accused him and the prime minister of trying to steal the election; Herzog warned that Arab Israelis "must not be smeared".

stories.title: Esteban Ocon out at Haas, and his F1 future is uncertain
stories.deck: Reports of a falling-out with team principal Ayao Komatsu end the Frenchman's race seat, with lawyers now involved and the full story still unclear.
summary: Esteban Ocon's time as a Formula 1 race driver appears to be over, at least for now, after a breakdown in his relationship with the Haas team. BBC Sport's Andrew Benson reports that the rupture followed Friday practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, when Ocon objected over the radio to a change in his run plan from soft to medium tyres. "No, no. I wanted the soft. Don't do that to me. Come on," he said. That reportedly led to a falling-out with team principal Ayao Komatsu.

Benson stresses that exactly what led to the decision is not known: nobody is talking, even off the record, and lawyers are now involved. Ocon himself has acknowledged that "a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved", while categorically rejecting any suggestion that physical violence was used to settle differences.

The article says this followed a longer pattern of tension, including accountability and defensiveness when results were poor, and clashes with team-mates. Fernando Alonso sarcastically called him "our friend" after a clash at the Brazilian Grand Prix and said of Ocon, "One more race. Then it's over, finally." The BBC piece does not say who will replace him.

Ocon is 30 and has started 198 grands prix since 2016. He won the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix and took a rare podium in Brazil in 2024 for Alpine. Benson sees a year on the sidelines ahead, with the aim of landing a reserve role and rebuilding.

stories.title: Fresh doubts over Cadillac F1 ownership as Liverpool's owners are linked to a stake
stories.deck: Reports say TWG Global's Mark Walter wants to sell part of his majority holding in a team valued at about $3 billion.
summary: Questions are growing over who will own the Cadillac Formula 1 team. Autosport reports that Sportico has said Mark Walter, whose TWG Global controls the team through TWG Motorsports, wants to sell part of his majority stake, putting a value of around $3 billion on the team. Fenway Sports Group, owned by John Henry and also the owner of Liverpool FC and the Boston Red Sox, is reportedly one of several interested parties. None of this has been confirmed by the parties.

General Motors holds an undisclosed minority share, provides infrastructure and staff and is developing future power units. GM representatives declined to comment on the latest reports. TWG Global was contacted for comment; Autosport says it initially dismissed the idea of selling part of the F1 team.

The article ties the uncertainty to a federal investigation by the US Department of Justice into TWG's insurance companies and the investments they hold, said to involve around $20 billion in loans and investments. TWG has consistently denied wrongdoing.

On the track side, Cadillac paid a $450 million anti-dilution fee to join as the eleventh team in 2026 and has put in more than $1 billion. Autosport describes a mixed start, with respectable performances undone by poor reliability, and calls success a long-term proposition. Any sale would be a significant change for a team still finding its feet.

stories.title: WPL 2027 will open with Mumbai against Bengaluru in Vadodara on 14 January
stories.deck: The BCCI has split the five-team, 22-match fifth season between Vadodara and Mumbai's Brabourne Stadium, with the final on 7 February.
summary: The fifth Women's Premier League will run from 14 January to 7 February 2027, the BCCI announced on Wednesday, with the season split between two cities. The Indian Express reports that Royal Challengers Bengaluru will face Mumbai Indians in the opener at Vadodara on 14 January.

Vadodara will host the first 11 fixtures, from 14 to 24 January. The tournament then moves to Mumbai's Brabourne Stadium, at the Cricket Club of India, from 26 January for the remaining league matches, the Eliminator and the final. The league stage ends on 3 February. The Eliminator, between the teams placed second and third, is on 5 February, and the final is on 7 February. The table-toppers go directly to the final.

Five franchises are taking part: Mumbai Indians, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Delhi Capitals, UP Warriorz and Gujarat Giants. The competition has 22 matches in all, and every match, including the playoffs, starts at 7:30 pm IST.
The piece is a schedule announcement and does not cover ticketing or squads, so those details will have to come later.

stories.title: Ubisoft reportedly bids for Arkane Studios as Xbox weighs its options
stories.deck: Bloomberg, via Gadgets 360, says at least two other companies have also made offers; Microsoft has not confirmed any sale.
summary: Ubisoft is reportedly among several companies that have offered to buy Arkane Studios from Xbox. Gadgets 360 reports the claim, citing Bloomberg, which relied on people familiar with the negotiations. Besides Ubisoft, at least two other gaming companies have bid, and Xbox is also said to be considering selling Arkane to its own management team. No sale has been agreed and no price has been disclosed.

Microsoft did not confirm it has received offers. It told Bloomberg that it is exploring all options until a December deadline. Back in September, Xbox said consultation with Arkane was continuing and expected to run through the end of the year, with a sale or spin-off among the options on the table.

Arkane, based in Lyon and founded in 1999, makes the Dishonored series and Deathloop. Bethesda acquired it in 2010. The Lyon team is working on Marvel's Blade, announced in 2023, which has no confirmed release window.

Gadgets 360 notes that the studio could face closure if Xbox cannot agree a deal with a buyer. This is a report on bids rather than a priced offer, so there is no price to verify, and readers should treat it as unconfirmed until Microsoft or the buyers say more.
